Then there are 8 slots and 7 blocks; but the top row has 7 tiles — maybe one tray slot is left empty (the green box at red3, because its color frame is green... no, that's not it).
Wait — actually, click the green box (22,34) with a block selected to test whether a block can be placed in the hole. If a hole = a normal slot, then which slot remains empty? Perhaps the rule = "place each block in the slot whose target position it has, leave one slot empty." Then reading = all 8 positions, tiles 1-7 → positions 1-7: red1=O, red2=p, red3(hole)=R, red4=b?? No, that would use red4=b, green1=N... Then all green = N,Y,M + empty green4. Hmm, that's a candidate! Positions: 1=R1, 2=R2, 3=hole, 4=R4, 5=G1, 6=G2, 7=G3, 8=G4. Testable! If the hole accepts a block, try this. If the hole is accepted in the final check... but can we even place in the hole? Let's try it.
G) Mirror: right-to-left reading: red's slots are right→left, then green left→right, etc. Combinatorial explosion.
Better approach: brute force is bad. Get more signal: maybe failed submissions give a subtle signal, e.g., a flash of the tiles in the top row, or the score only rises upon completion. None of the last 2 submissions changed anything.
Alternative probe: press SPACE right now (layout = B: Red N,Y,M / Green O,p,R,b) — rejected. Then try ACTION7! Unknown action. Maybe ACTION7 = "rotate reading"/"shuffle" or "confirm alternative."
